title: Adam and Eve in the Garden

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: God shaped the first man out of the earth and gave him breath, and the man became a living soul. Then God planted a garden in Eden, toward the east, and put the man there to work it and keep it. Every tree that was good to look at and good for food grew there.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: God gave the man one boundary. He could eat freely from every tree in the garden except one: the tree that gave the knowledge of good and evil. If he ate from that tree, he would die.

verses.text: And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: God brought the animals to the man, and the man gave each one its name. But among them all, there was no partner suited to him. So God caused a deep sleep to fall on him, took one of his ribs, and made a woman, and brought her to the man.

verses.text: And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.

segments.speaker: adam
segments.text: This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: They were together in the garden, and they had nothing to hide from each other or from God.

verses.text: Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the LORD God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the LORD God had made. And he said unto the woman,

segments.speaker: serpent
segments.text: Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Notice how the question twists what God said. God had given them every tree but one. The serpent made it sound as if God had held everything back.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The woman answered that they could eat from the trees, but not from the tree in the middle of the garden, or they would die.

verses.text: And the serpent said unto the woman, Ye shall not surely die:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the serpent said unto the woman,

verses.text: For God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.

segments.speaker: serpent
segments.text: For God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.

verses.text: And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: In a single moment, everything changed. Their eyes were opened, and they knew they were naked. They sewed fig leaves together to cover themselves. Then, in the cool of the day, they heard God walking in the garden, and they hid from him among the trees.

verses.text: And the LORD God called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where art thou?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the LORD God called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where art thou?

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: God knew where Adam was. The question was an invitation to come out.

verses.text: And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself.

segments.speaker: adam
segments.text: I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: God asked whether he had eaten from the tree he had been told not to eat from.

verses.text: And the man said, The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.

segments.speaker: adam
segments.text: The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.

verses.text: And the LORD God said unto the woman, What is this that thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the LORD God said unto the woman, What is this that thou hast done? And the woman said,

segments.speaker: eve
segments.text: The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The man blamed the woman, and even seemed to blame God for giving her to him. The woman blamed the serpent. People have been passing blame ever since.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: There were consequences. Life outside the garden would be hard. Work would be sweat and struggle, and in the end they would return to the dust they came from. Adam named his wife Eve, the mother of everyone who would ever live.

verses.text: Unto Adam also and to his wife did the LORD God make coats of skins, and clothed them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Unto Adam also and to his wife did the LORD God make coats of skins, and clothed them.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Before they left the garden, God made them clothes of skins and dressed them himself. Their choices were real, and so was their loss. But even as they went out of Eden, God was still caring for them.

first_reader.note: Drafted and read by Claude in the landing session; no free-model draft (QA_NO_FREE_MODEL not needed).

pastor.note: Faithful to Genesis 2:7-3:23; no doctrine of the fall added; God's questions read as the text gives them; ends on God clothing them.

cultural.note: Neither the man nor the woman is made the villain; the blame-passing is named for both.
